newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: More than 100,000 Serbians join church-led protest.
newsitem.headline: More than 100,000 Serbians join church-led protest.

text.p: More than 100,000 people crowded into central Belgrade on Monday for a religious procession and pro-democracy march led by the Serbian Orthodox church, witnesses said.
Patriarch Pavle began the procession at 7.30 a.m. (0630 GMT) in front of the Serbian Orthodox Cathedral in the city centre, flanked by some 20 priests chanting hymns.

The march, called by the powerful church to mark Saint Sava day, began just hours after up to 50,000 students and their supporters swept triumphantly through the city when riot police withdrew a cordon that had prevented them from marching for eight days.
In contrast to the boisterous, whistle-blowing students who celebrated their victory by marching for three hours, the church procession was quiet apart from the chanting of the priests.

The church's involvement stepped up the pressure on the government of Socialist President Slobodan Milosevic to acknowledge victories by the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition in municipal elections last November.
The opposition victories in 14 cities, including the capital Belgrade, were annulled by the government, but Milosevic has been under strong pressure from the West to reinstate them.
